deck.title: EventBridge & Step Functions
deck.analogy: EventBridge is a railway switchboard operator routing trains (events) to the right track; Step Functions is the station master running one planned journey with a logbook.

subtopics.title: EventBridge: the event router of AWS

cards.front: What is Amazon EventBridge?

back.answer: A serverless event bus (formerly CloudWatch Events) that receives JSON events and matches them against rules to route them to targets.
back.explanation: Same engine as CloudWatch Events with a bigger brand.

cards.front: What is AWS Step Functions?

back.answer: A workflow orchestrator: you define a state machine (a JSON flowchart) coordinating Lambda and other services step by step.
back.explanation: It runs one planned journey start to finish and logs every step.
back.mnemonic: Step Functions = station master with a clipboard.

cards.front: What are the three parts of the EventBridge flow?

back.answer: Sources → event bus with rules (pattern match) → targets.
back.explanation: Rules decide whether an event's pattern matches and where it goes.

cards.sourceHeading: EventBridge: the event router of AWS

cards.front: What event sources can feed EventBridge?

back.answer: AWS services, SaaS partners (Zendesk, Datadog, Auth0, Shopify) via partner event bus, and custom apps using PutEvents.

cards.sourceHeading: EventBridge: the event router of AWS

cards.front: What is EventBridge's signature filtering capability?

back.answer: Content-based filtering: rules match on any field of the event JSON, including deep in the payload.

cards.sourceHeading: EventBridge: the event router of AWS

cards.front: Which targets can an EventBridge rule send to?

back.answer: Lambda, SQS, SNS, Step Functions, Kinesis, ECS tasks, another event bus, and more; one rule can fan to multiple targets.

cards.sourceHeading: EventBridge: the event router of AWS

cards.front: How do you run a Lambda every night at 2 AM in EventBridge terms?

back.answer: A scheduled rule (cron or rate expression) targeting Lambda: serverless cron.
back.explanation: No EC2 instance running crontab; that is always the wrong answer.

cards.sourceHeading: EventBridge: the event router of AWS

cards.front: What does EventBridge archive + replay do?

back.answer: Records events on a bus and replays them later, e.g. to reprocess after a bug fix.

cards.sourceHeading: EventBridge: the event router of AWS

cards.front: What is the EventBridge schema registry for?

back.answer: It discovers event structures and generates code bindings so developers know what fields to expect.

cards.sourceHeading: EventBridge: the event router of AWS

cards.front: How do you centralize events from many accounts using EventBridge?

back.answer: Cross-account event buses: send events from account A's bus to account B's bus.

cards.sourceHeading: EventBridge: the event router of AWS

cards.front: EventBridge vs SNS: which one for SaaS routing/content filtering vs huge fan-out?

back.answer: EventBridge: content filtering, AWS/SaaS event routing, scheduling, archive/replay. SNS: massive fan-out push (mobile, SMS, email).
back.explanation: Both send events to targets, so exams bait you.

cards.sourceHeading: EventBridge: the event router of AWS

cards.front: Step Functions Task state: what does it do?

back.answer: Does work: invokes Lambda, ECS, DynamoDB, etc. The worker step.

cards.front: Which Step Functions state handles if/else branching?

back.explanation: Cue: different path based on result.

cards.front: Which Step Functions state pauses for a time or until a timestamp?
Which Step Functions state runs branches at the same time?
Which Step Functions state does a for-each over an array?

back.explanation: Cue: process each item in a list.

cards.front: Which Step Functions feature gives exponential backoff retries without custom code?

back.answer: Retry/Catch, built into the state definition.
back.explanation: "Retry with backoff without custom code" → Step Functions.

cards.front: Fragile Lambda A→B→C chain, over 15 minutes, needs error handling and audit: what is the answer?

back.answer: Step Functions orchestrating the Lambdas, never Lambdas calling Lambdas.
back.explanation: You get visual workflow, per-step retry, and full execution history; Lambda's 15-minute cap is per function.

cards.front: What is the max duration of Step Functions Standard vs Express workflows?
How are Step Functions Standard and Express priced?

back.answer: Standard: per state transition. Express: per execution/duration, cheaper at volume.

cards.front: Step Functions Standard vs Express: execution history?

back.answer: Standard: full audit history in the console. Express: CloudWatch Logs only.

cards.front: Step Functions Standard vs Express: best fit?

back.answer: Standard: long-running, human approval, audit-heavy. Express: high-volume, short (IoT ingestion, streaming).
back.explanation: Hundreds of thousands of short IoT events per second, cost-sensitive → Express.

cards.front: Run a cleanup Lambda every night at 2 AM without managing servers. Which solution?
Ingest events from Zendesk/Datadog into AWS and route them to Lambda. Which service?

back.explanation: SaaS integration is EventBridge's exclusive turf.

cards.front: Order workflow needs retries, error handling, and a manual approval step that may take days. Which?

choices.why: Supports up to 1 year and approvals.

cards.front: A multi-step pipeline of Lambdas exceeds 15 minutes end to end. What do you use?

back.explanation: Lambda's 15-minute cap is per function; the workflow can run far longer.

cards.front: Process each item in an array of records as a separate step. Which Step Functions feature?
Need an audit trail with input/output of every step of each execution. Which?
Route only events where a specific JSON field matches a value to different targets. Which?
Millions of short-lived, high-frequency workflow executions at lowest cost. Which?
Reprocess last week's events after fixing a bug. Which EventBridge feature?
Retry a failing step with exponential backoff, no custom retry code. Which?

back.answer: Step Functions Retry, built into the state definition.
